title: Signature System Model Record
body:
Overview

This record belongs to the Advanced Control Theory Signature Database (Signature edition), Manon's original counterpart to the public database of the same name. The Signature edition does not copy any public product: it restates the subject in Manon's own Signature framing, as a design that lives inside the Signature ecosystem. System Model Record covers the following in Signature terms: stores one system model with its parameters, assumptions, and stated limits. The record is written as a complete, usable file, with a demo program genuinely executed at build time and its output stored beside the code. Design targets only: labels in this record describe design targets for engineering work, never a claim of NASA, DARPA, or contractor qualification or approval.

How the Signature design works

The Signature design works like this: a control record starts from a system model, derives a controller design from it, checks stability from the closed-loop poles and margins, and evaluates disturbance response, with every calculation shown so it can be rechecked. Applied to this record, the design means the following in practice: stores one system model with its parameters, assumptions, and stated limits. The record sits at ladder rank simple in the teaching ladder, which runs simple, then compounded, then most complex, so a Signature reader can start from the simpler records and work toward this one.

Worked example

The demo checks closed-loop poles and prints stability under the stated model with gain and phase margins. The demo program prints:

Closed-loop poles: [-1.0, -2.0, -0.5]
Stable under stated model: True
Gain margin: 6, phase margin: 30 degrees

Use and limits

A stability verdict holds for the stated model only. Real hardware adds delays, saturation, and unmodeled dynamics that can overturn a paper verdict, so model limits are always recorded beside the result. In Signature practice, a reader can use this record to run the same check inside the Signature ecosystem: follow the design, compare the result with the worked example, and record any difference with its evidence. The record is one of sixteen in this Signature database, and it cross-links to related databases so the reader can continue from here.

Record details
